findings.text: stream_carries admits rows by state family and has no clause for gate-running/gate-ended, and transition_class(None, 'gate-running') returns ROW_OBSERVER, so the follower's row policy drops every gate row the new fold writes; the node's goal is to show the gate on the pane and no pane will draw it.

the assertion that no row carries OTHER_SESSION can never fail: OTHER_SESSION is never passed to any code under test, so a sweep that mis-scoped rows to a different session would still leave this line true, and the done_when's 'none for another session' case is not actually guarded by it.

the fragment cites 87 related files and 644 passed with no added failure, but no surviving log carries that run: related-suite.log now holds a different 60-file run of 1034 passed, 2 failed, so a reader cannot reconcile the artifact's gate result with the manifest or the log it points at.

baseline_suite records a three-test targeted command while after_suite records the 60-file related population, so the base arm does not measure the file set the evidence fence names; the zero added-failure count still holds only because the after arm's two failures are the two ids that base arm also fails.

the new module copies lift_watch._append_rows and lift_watch._aware verbatim (reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:230 and :247) instead of importing them, so the stream-path default and the naive-datetime normalisation now have two copies that can drift.

item_verdicts.goal: VERDICT goal: the goal is to show a coordinator's own verify-gate and suite run gates as rows on its pane; reckon/crew/gate_watch.py writes the record and folds rows, but reckon/crew/ticker.py:1428 drops them.
item_verdicts.manifest: VERDICT manifest: read; states the node gate passed 5 cases, the negative control failed the start-record case, and the 60-file related run added no failure against base.
